question: What form of initiation arises when the teacher properly looks at the disciple?
premises: The teacher looks properly at the disciple.
This gaze functions as an initiatory act.
The resulting initiation is identified as sight-initiation.
inference: When the teacher properly sees the disciple, this becomes sight-initiation.
plain_english: Dear one, if the teacher properly looks at the disciple, this becomes initiation by sight.
